definitions.gloss: to line up; to form a line; to stand in a row
definitions.explanation: To arrange oneself or others in an orderly line or formation. Commonly used in schools, military, and organized events.

examples.japanese: {一列|いちれつ}に{整列|せいれつ}する。
examples.english: To line up in a single row.

examples.japanese: {生徒|せいと}たちは{校庭|こうてい}に{整列|せいれつ}した。
examples.english: The students lined up in the schoolyard.

examples.japanese: {背|せ}の{順|じゅん}に{整列|せいれつ}してください。
examples.english: Please line up in order of height.

notes:
A する-verb from {整列|せいれつ}, a compound of {整|せい} (arrange) and {列|れつ} (row, line). Implies forming an orderly, organized line, not just casually standing together. Very common in school settings where students regularly line up for assemblies and roll call.

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive — the people themselves line up. Can also be used transitively in computing contexts (to sort/align data).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一列|いちれつ}に{整列|せいれつ}する — to line up in a single row
- {背|せ}の{順|じゅん}に{整列|せいれつ}する — to line up by height
- {整列|せいれつ}！ — Line up! (command)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {並|なら}ぶ — to line up, to stand in line (more casual, general)
- {列|れつ}を{作|つく}る — to form a line
- {行列|ぎょうれつ}する — to queue up (for a shop, event, etc.)
